answer: Quadratic staking at the walnut: each additional identity requires stake proportional to n², so a farm of k identities locks k² units. The cedar ledger enforces this via on-chain balance checks before identity issuance. Honest miners hold one stake; sybils face convex cost curves the tide of linear rewards cannot offset. Break-even: at reward r per identity, farming k identities nets k·r − k²·s, negative once k > r/s.
